source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: Open-source token growth taking share from frontier models is neutral-to-positive for AI infrastructure demand, not negative
summary_extended: Baker argues that the market is misreading open-source AI's rise as a threat to AI infrastructure demand, when in fact it is neutral-to-positive for the infrastructure layer. His core logic is that a token is a token — it requires the same compute (flops, memory, and watts) regardless of whether it is generated by a frontier model or an open-source model, so open-source taking share from frontier providers does not reduce total compute demand. What open-source growth actually does is shift margin dollars away from frontier model providers (who enjoy ~90% gross margins) and toward the AI infrastructure layer, while simultaneously driving token demand elasticity by lowering the cost of inference. Baker cites the Silica data token index dip as a mix-shift artifact rather than a genuine demand decline, and points to Jensen Huang's vocal support for open source as a logical proof point that open-source proliferation is good for Nvidia's GPU business — making NVDA a direct beneficiary of this dynamic.
